chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Imran ibn Zabyan, from Hakim ibn Saad, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said:
The companions of the Mahdi will be young men; there will be no old men among them except like the kohl in the eye or the salt in the provisions, and the least part of the provisions is the salt.
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the companions of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the demographic composition of the Mahdi's companions, using the simile of kohl in the eye and salt in provisions to illustrate that the elderly will be extremely few, much like the minimal quantity of these essential yet minor ingredients. This imagery underscores a generation defined by vigor and readiness for action, while the few elders serve as wise, stabilizing figures rather than the majority. The metaphor reflects the Shia understanding of a transitional era where youthful energy drives the establishment of justice, guided by the scarce but crucial wisdom of the aged.
